step_by_step_reasoning: We identify the nodes directly from the whiteboard icons: Transit Gateway, ELB, EC2 (representing K8s worker nodes), CloudWatch, S3, and RDS. A handwritten OnPrem DC representing Texas/Washington data centers connects to Transit Gateway. Users access the applications via ELB. Standard flows route traffic from User -> ELB -> EC2, EC2 -> RDS for database operations, EC2 -> Transit Gateway -> On-Prem DC for datacenter connectivity, and EC2 -> CloudWatch for observability.

edges.notes: Users send HTTPS requests to the application endpoints.
ELB forwards traffic to the Kubernetes containers running on EC2.
Applications run queries and store persistent state in RDS.
Clusters route cross-account or cross-VPC traffic.
Transit Gateway bridges AWS infrastructure to Texas/Washington data centers.
Prometheus forwards telemetry, metrics, and alerts to CloudWatch.
